posts.title: Design team appointed for injury unit
posts.description: A design team has been appointed to advance plans for the proposed Minor Injury Unit on the grounds of St Columbanus Home though the HSE has confirmed it cannot yet give a construction or opening timeline. Fianna Fáil TD Deputy Michael Cahill received the update in response to a Parliamentary Question submitted to the Minister for Health. HSE South West confirmed the newly appointed team will progress the project through design development, planning, and regulatory approval following the transfer of residents to the new Killarney Community Nursing Unit. Deputy Cahill welcomed the appointment of the design team but raised concerns over the lack of a definitive schedule. “I welcome the appointment of a design team, which represents progress towards delivering this important facility. However, I am concerned that the HSE is still unable to provide a definitive timeline. posts.title: Lochanna Beo’s mapping highlights water quality concerns
posts.description: Lochanna Beo’s mapping highlights water quality concerns Local environmental action group Lochanna Beo has released mapping data from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to draw attention to deteriorating water quality across Killarney and the broader Laune Catchment. The EPA map uses a colour-coded system to rate water quality status from 2019 to 2024: blue indicates high status, green indicates good, yellow represents moderate, brown denotes poor, and red signifies bad status. The figures indicate significant ecological pressure on local lakes and rivers compared to neighbouring areas across County Kerry. Formed during the summer of 2026, Lochanna Beo aims to bring together residents, business owners, agricultural operators, and public bodies to address the key factors affecting the regional aquatic ecosystem. posts.title: Stefan Caulfield-Dreier signs professional cycling contract
posts.description: Former Killarney Cycling Club rider Stefan Caulfield-Dreier has secured a professional contract with leading Dutch-based outfit Azerion-Villa Valkenburg. The 23-year-old Beaufort native began his cycling career with Killarney Cycling Club in the under-12 age category. He demonstrated strong potential during his youth career, culminating in a victory at the Under-16 National Time-Trial Championship in 2019. After progressing through the junior ranks, Caulfield-Dreier began racing on the Continent with a Dutch squad upon entering senior competition. He claimed Senior National Track titles in both the Points and Madison events in 2023 and 2024, and went on to represent Ireland at international track events in the Netherlands and Switzerland across 2024 and 2025. Announcing the signing, team management at Azerion-Villa Valkenburg highlighted Caulfield-Dreier as a specialist in classics and time trials who excels in demanding race conditions.
